external_entities.name: developer
external_entities.description: A developer who pushes branches and can log in to the build runner to start a rebuild.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server
external_entities.notes: The text does not state where developers are located or what trust zone they occupy.

external_entities.name: public package registry
external_entities.description: The public package registry reached during dependency resolution.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet

processes.name: build runner
processes.description: Picks up merges, fetches source, resolves the dependency lockfile, produces container images, pushes images to the registry, calls the deploy controller, and can be used by developers to start rebuilds.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.
processes.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on downloads from the public package registry.

processes.name: deploy controller
processes.description: Maintains the current release image SHA for the estate and answers store server queries about the current release.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network and holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on.
processes.notes: The text says the runner uses a shared build token to call the controller, and that what store servers present to the controller has not been documented.

processes.name: store server
processes.description: A small server in each store's back office that asks for the current release, pulls a different image when needed, and restarts the till software container.
processes.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
processes.notes: There are about 1,200 store servers. What a store server presents to the registry and deploy controller has not been documented.

processes.name: till software
processes.description: Till software running as a container on each store server.
processes.source_excerpt: running the till software as a container
processes.notes: The text does not describe an interface presented by the till software.

data_stores.name: git server
data_stores.description: A self-hosted git server containing developer branches and the source fetched by the build runner.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the git server encrypts what it stores.

data_stores.name: image registry
data_stores.description: A registry in the build environment that stores finished container images tagged with commit SHAs and serves images to store servers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry, which is also in the build environment.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the image registry encrypts what it stores. The registry allows store-server pulls, but what a store server presents to it has not been documented.

data_flows.name: push branches
data_flows.description: A developer pushes a branch to the git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

data_flows.name: trigger build
data_flows.description: The git server starts a build when a merge to main occurs.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A merge to `main` is what starts a build.
data_flows.data_description: merge to main and build trigger

data_flows.name: fetch source
data_flows.description: The build runner fetches source from the git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source

data_flows.name: resolve dependencies
data_flows.description: The build runner reaches out to the public package registry during dependency resolution.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_flows.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.

data_flows.name: push image
data_flows.description: The build runner pushes a finished container image to the image registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_flows.data_description: finished container image tagged with the commit SHA

data_flows.name: set release
data_flows.description: The build runner asks the deploy controller to make an image the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release
data_flows.notes: The runner uses a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.

data_flows.name: query release
data_flows.description: A store server asks the deploy controller for the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.notes: What a store server presents to the deploy controller has not been documented.

data_flows.name: pull image
data_flows.description: A store server pulls the current container image from the image registry when its running image differs.
data_flows.source_excerpt: if it differs from what it is running it pulls that image from the registry
data_flows.notes: The registry allows the pull, but what a store server presents to it has not been documented.
data_flows.data_description: container image tagged with the commit SHA

data_flows.name: kick off rebuild
data_flows.description: A developer logs in to the build runner and starts a rebuild of main without a merge.
data_flows.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
data_flows.notes: This path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where the self-hosted git server and deploy controller run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the self-hosted git server, which sits on the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: build environment
trust_boundaries.description: The separate build environment containing the build runner and image registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The runner lives in its own build environment, separate from the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: store estate
trust_boundaries.description: The estate of approximately 1,200 stores containing the store servers.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The image registry is reachable from the store estate over the WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: retail WAN
trust_boundaries.description: The WAN carrying traffic between the stores and the corporate network.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Traffic between the stores and the corporate network goes over the retail WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public internet where the public package registry is located.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the public package registry on the internet

assumptions.assumption: The developer carries or handles source and build-related business data and credentials when interacting with the pipeline.
assumptions.basis: Developers push branches, log in to the build runner, and initiate rebuilds.

assumptions.assumption: The public package registry carries business-critical data because it supplies dependency packages used to produce the container image.
assumptions.basis: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry and the resulting dependencies are used in the build.

assumptions.assumption: The build runner handles business-critical data and credentials.
assumptions.basis: It fetches source, resolves dependencies, produces images, pushes images, and uses the shared build token.

assumptions.assumption: The deploy controller handles business-critical data and credentials.
assumptions.basis: It holds the estate's current image SHA and receives the shared build token from the runner.

assumptions.assumption: The store server handles business-critical data.
assumptions.basis: It retrieves and runs the current till-software container image for the store estate.

assumptions.assumption: The till software handles business-critical data.
assumptions.basis: It is the till software running on the store servers.

assumptions.assumption: The git server stores confidential source and build material.
assumptions.basis: The git server stores developer branches and source code.

assumptions.assumption: The image registry stores confidential container images.
assumptions.basis: The image registry stores finished container images produced from the source.

assumptions.assumption: The developer-to-git-server flow carries business-critical data.
assumptions.basis: The flow carries developer branches and source code.

assumptions.assumption: The git-server-to-build-runner flow carries business-critical data.
assumptions.basis: The interaction carries a merge to main that starts a build.

assumptions.assumption: The build-runner-to-git-server flow carries business-critical data.
assumptions.basis: The flow carries source code and the dependency lockfile.

assumptions.assumption: The build-runner-to-public-package-registry flow carries business-critical data.
assumptions.basis: The flow carries dependency packages used by the build.

assumptions.assumption: The build-runner-to-image-registry flow carries business-critical data.
assumptions.basis: The flow carries a finished container image.

assumptions.assumption: The build-runner-to-deploy-controller flow carries business-critical data and credentials.
assumptions.basis: The flow carries the image SHA and the shared build token.

assumptions.assumption: The store-server-to-deploy-controller flow carries business-critical data.
assumptions.basis: The flow carries the current release image SHA.

assumptions.assumption: The store-server-to-image-registry flow carries business-critical data.
assumptions.basis: The flow carries a container image.

assumptions.assumption: The developer-to-build-runner flow carries business-critical data and credentials.
assumptions.basis: The developer logs in to the runner and submits a rebuild request for main.
